termixId.title: Termix ID
termixId.claimIntro: Pick a unique handle. Your SSH public keys will be published at a public URL you can add to any server's authorized_keys file.
termixId.deleteConfirm: Delete your Termix ID and all published keys? Servers you provisioned will keep the keys until you remove them manually.
termixId.generateTooltip: Generate an Ed25519 key pair — publishes the public key and downloads the private key to your device
termixId.importFromCredential: Or import from a stored credential
termixId.generatedSaved: Key pair generated and saved to your credentials vault. Private key also downloaded.
termixId.generatedOnly: Key pair generated — private key downloaded (shown only once).
termixId.caIntro: Trust this CA on a server and it accepts any certificate you sign. Rotate to revoke everything at once; certificates also expire on their own.
termixId.caTrustLabel: Trust on a server (run as root)
termixId.caRotateConfirm: Rotate the CA? Every certificate it has signed will stop being accepted and must be re-issued.
termixId.issueCertTooltip: Issue an SSH certificate for this key, signed by your CA

credentials.caCertificateDescription: Optional: Upload or paste the CA-signed certificate file (e.g. id_ed25519-cert.pub). Required when your SSH server uses certificate-based authorization.
credentials.noPublicKeyAvailable: No public key available. Open the credential editor first.

share.title: Share "{{name}}"
share.description: Recipients get their own encrypted copy of the secrets. It is refreshed whenever the credential changes and removed when the share is revoked.
share.levelUseDesc: Use: attach the credential to hosts and connect. The secret itself stays hidden.
share.levelManageDesc: Manage: also edit the credential and share it with others.

credentials.customizeSidebarDescription: Choose how the credential list looks and behaves.
credentials.densityComfortableDesc: One credential per row, with extra detail.
credentials.densityCompactDesc: One line per credential, for longer lists.
credentials.showCredentialTagsDesc: Display tags in the credential list
credentials.actionsVisibilityDesc: When the connection and management buttons on each credential show up
credentials.customizeSortHint: Sort order lives in the sort menu in the toolbar.
credentials.arrangeUnlockedSwitchedToManual: Switched to manual sort so your order sticks

serverConfig.title: Server Configuration
serverConfig.description: Configure the Termix server URL to connect to your backend services
serverConfig.helpText: Enter the URL where your Termix server is running (e.g., http://localhost:30001 or https://your-server.com)
serverConfig.mustIncludeProtocol: Server URL must start with http:// or https://
serverConfig.allowInvalidCertificateDesc: Use only for trusted self-hosted servers with self-signed or IP-address certificates.
serverConfig.embeddedDesc: Run Termix with the built-in local server (no remote server needed)
serverConfig.embeddedNotReady: Local server is not ready yet. Please wait a moment and try again.

migrationNotice.title: Termix Desktop now runs standalone
migrationNotice.body1: This app used to connect straight to your Termix server. It's been reworked to run fully on its own, storing hosts and credentials locally so it keeps working offline. Two-way sync with a self-hosted Termix server is now optional.
migrationNotice.body2: Your existing hosts and credentials are still on {{url}}. Turn on Remote Sync and reconnect to that server to bring them back and keep both in sync going forward.

remoteSync.title: Remote Sync
remoteSync.description: Optionally connect this desktop app to a self-hosted Termix server to sync your hosts, credentials, and snippets across devices. The app always works fully offline whether or not you connect.
remoteSync.syncUnavailable: Remote sync could not be started
remoteSync.mustIncludeProtocol: Server URL must start with http:// or https://
remoteSync.connectionTestFailed: Could not reach a Termix server at that URL
remoteSync.allowInvalidCertificateDesc: Use only for trusted self-hosted servers with self-signed or IP-address certificates.
remoteSync.originDescription: Choose where SSH connections originate from by default. This can be overridden per host.

versionCheck.updateLinkLabel: Update available — open the release notes on GitHub
versionCheck.newVersionAvailable: A new version is available! You are running {{current}}, but {{latest}} is available.
versionCheck.betaVersionDesc: You are running {{current}}, which is newer than the latest stable release {{latest}}.

onboarding.welcomeIntro: Termix manages your servers from one place. This setup takes about a minute and nothing here is permanent.
onboarding.welcome_hosts_desc: Keep every machine you manage in one list.
onboarding.welcome_terminal_desc: Open a terminal in a tab, no separate SSH client.
onboarding.welcome_files_desc: Upload, download and edit remote files.
onboarding.presetTitle: How much do you want on screen?
onboarding.presetIntro: Termix can be as simple or as detailed as you like. Pick a starting point.
onboarding.presetChangeLater: You can switch presets or change any single setting later in Settings, under Interface.
onboarding.appearanceIntro: Pick a theme, an accent color and your language. All three can be changed later in Settings.
onboarding.featuresIntro: Every server you save can be opened in more than a terminal. Here is what is waiting behind the icons on the left.
onboarding.feature_files_desc: Browse, upload, download and edit files over SFTP without leaving the app.
onboarding.feature_tunnels_desc: Forward ports through a server to reach services that are not exposed.
onboarding.featuresRailHint: Do not need one of these? Hide any icon from the sidebar in Settings, under Navigation.
onboarding.workflowIntro: A few habits that save the most time once you have a couple of servers.
onboarding.workflow_palette_desc: Jump to any server or action by typing. Tap Shift twice to open it.
onboarding.workflow_split_desc: Show up to four tabs side by side to watch logs while you work.
onboarding.workflow_dock_desc: Middle click or right click a sidebar icon to open it as a tab or pin it to the right.
onboarding.securityIntro: Termix stores credentials for you, so it is worth a minute to see how that works.
onboarding.security_credentials_desc: Save a key or password once and attach it to as many servers as you like.
onboarding.security_twofa_desc: Add TOTP or a passkey to your account in Settings, under Security.
onboarding.security_identity_desc: Issue short lived SSH certificates instead of copying keys to every server.
onboarding.security_sharing_desc: Give other users access to a server without handing over the password.
onboarding.securityEncryptionNote: Credentials are encrypted before they are stored, and only decrypted when a connection needs them.
onboarding.doneDesc: Pick a server from the sidebar to open a terminal, browse its files or see its metrics.
onboarding.done_settings_desc: Themes, layout density and which icons show up all live in Settings.
onboarding.done_rerun_desc: Open Settings, go to Interface and choose Run setup to walk through these steps again.
onboarding.done_desktop_desc: Termix runs as a desktop app on Windows, macOS and Linux.
onboarding.done_mobile_desc: Take your servers with you on iOS and Android.
onboarding.done_docs_desc: Guides for every feature, including ones not covered here.
onboarding.done_cli_desc: Manage your servers from a terminal, and use Termix in your own scripts.

nav.openAsTabHint: Ctrl+click or middle click to open as a tab
nav.multiPanelHintTitle: Work with more than one panel
nav.multiPanelHintBody: Keep this panel open while the sidebar is used for something else. Two ways to move it:
nav.multiPanelHintTabHow: Ctrl+click its rail icon, or use the button in this header.
nav.multiPanelHintDockHow: Right-click its rail icon, or use the panel icon in the tab bar.

hosts.unsavedChangesDescription: Your host changes have not been saved. Discard them?
hosts.overrideCredentialUsernameDesc: Use the username specified above instead of the credential's username
hosts.oidcUsernameHint: Use $oidc.preferred_username to substitute your OIDC login name.
hosts.pinToTopDesc: Always show this host at the top of the list
hosts.useSocks5ProxyDesc: Route connection through a proxy server
hosts.connectionOriginDesc: Where this host's connection originates from. Overrides the desktop app's global default.
hosts.authenticationMethodDesc: Select the one method Termix will use to authenticate this SSH connection. Other methods are not tried automatically.
hosts.vaultProfileHint: Settings come from the shared profile; you'll sign in to Vault via OIDC when you connect. No secrets are stored.
hosts.vaultProfileValidationError: Name, Vault address and SSH signer role are required
hosts.keyReplaceNotice: paste a new key below to replace it
hosts.stepcaDesc: Sign in through your identity provider and let your Step CA issue a short-lived SSH certificate for this host. The CA URL, root fingerprint and OIDC provisioner are set by an administrator under Admin Settings.
hosts.agentDesc: Authenticate using an SSH agent running on the Termix server (Bitwarden, 1Password, gpg-agent, KeeAgent, ssh-agent). The agent must be running on the machine where Termix is hosted.
hosts.agentAuthenticationDesc: Use keys from an SSH agent to authenticate this connection. Leave the socket path empty to use SSH_AUTH_SOCK.
hosts.agentSocketPathHint: Leave empty to auto-detect from the SSH_AUTH_SOCK environment variable, or enter a custom socket path (e.g. /run/user/1000/gnupg/S.gpg-agent.ssh).
hosts.agentIdentityPlaceholder: Leave empty to try all keys from the agent
hosts.agentIdentityHint: Paste a public key (e.g. ssh-ed25519 AAAA...) to only offer that key from the agent. Recommended when the agent holds many keys, to avoid exceeding the server's MaxAuthTries.
hosts.shareSshAuthDesc: Give recipients encrypted copies of this host's SSH authentication. A recipient's personal credential still takes precedence.
hosts.forceKeyboardInteractiveShortDesc: Force manual password entry even if keys are present
hosts.allowLegacyAlgorithmsDesc: Enable deprecated SSH algorithms (ssh-dss, ssh-rsa, diffie-hellman-group1-sha1, hmac-md5, 3des-cbc) for connections to old devices that cannot be upgraded.
hosts.fontFamilyCustomPlaceholder: Exact font name, e.g. MesloLGS NF
hosts.fontFamilyCustomHint: Pick a bundled font, or choose Custom and type the exact name of a font already installed on your system (e.g. MesloLGS NF, Noto Sans Mono). Termix cannot install fonts for you, install it on your OS first.
hosts.cursorBlinkingDesc: Enable blinking animation for the terminal cursor
hosts.rightClickSelectsWordShortDesc: Select the word under cursor on right-click
hosts.macOptionIsMetaShortDesc: Disable to type special characters (like @ or |) with the Option/Alt key on macOS instead of sending Meta
hosts.backgroundImageDesc: Optional URL for a terminal background image
hosts.saveGlobalThemeNamePrompt: Enter a name for this theme
hosts.syntaxHighlightingDesc: Colorize terminal output (errors, paths, IPs, timestamps)
hosts.syntaxHighlightingCategoriesDesc: Choose which types of content to colorize
hosts.scrollbackMaxLines: Maximum number of lines kept in history
hosts.sshAgentForwardingShortDesc: Allow this remote host to use your local SSH agent for onward connections. This is not required for Agent authentication.
hosts.useSSHTitleDesc: Update the tab title from the shell's window title instead of the host name
hosts.enableAutoMoshDesc: Prefer Mosh over SSH if available
hosts.enableAutoTmuxDesc: Keep your shell and anything running in it alive across disconnects and browser restarts by running inside tmux (tmux must be installed on the host)
hosts.localEchoDesc: Predict safe printable keystrokes locally on slow connections. Password prompts and control input are never echoed.
hosts.linkClickBehaviorDesc: Controls what happens when you click a link in the terminal. Use 'Default' to follow the app-level setting.
hosts.linkClickBehaviorConfirm: Show popup to open or copy
hosts.sudoPasswordAutoFillShortDesc: Automatically provide sudo password when prompted
hosts.sudoPasswordAutoFillDesc: Store a sudo password so host metrics, terminal prompts, and others can run privileged commands automatically.
hosts.showConnectionToolbarDesc: Show the toolbar in this host's SSH, RDP, VNC, and Telnet sessions. You can also hide it temporarily from the toolbar itself.
hosts.proxmoxStatsUrlCopied: Proxmox Stats URL copied to clipboard
hosts.enableStatusChecksDesc: Periodically ping this host to verify availability
hosts.useGlobalIntervalDesc: Override with the server-wide status check interval
hosts.cpuUsageDesc: CPU percent, load averages, sparkline graph
hosts.listeningPortsDesc: Open ports with process and state
hosts.credentialNameRequired: Please enter a name for the credential
hosts.credentialAuthRequired: Add a password, an SSH key, or both
hosts.createCredentialFromHostDesc: Create a reusable, shareable credential entry prefilled with this host's current username, password, and/or SSH key.
hosts.addFirstHost: Add your first host to get started
hosts.saveCredentialAsNewDesc: Creates a new credential with these changes and assigns it to this host. The original credential is left unchanged.
hosts.failedToSaveCredentialAsNew: Failed to save as a new credential
hosts.deleteAllInFolder: Delete all hosts in "{{name}}"? This cannot be undone.
hosts.cannotNestUnderDescendant: Can't nest a host under its own sub-host
hosts.folderDialogDescription: Choose a name, color, and icon. Use / to nest folders.
hosts.folderNestingHint: Use / to separate levels and create nested folders.
hosts.folderNameDuplicate: A folder with this name already exists here.
hosts.folderCredentialHint: Hosts in this folder that use "Stored credential" auth without their own credential selected will inherit this one.
hosts.deleteFolderConfirm: Delete "{{name}}" and its {{count}} host(s)? This cannot be undone.
hosts.customizeSidebarDescription: Choose how the host list looks and behaves.
hosts.customizeSortHint: Sort order and grouping live in the sort and group menus in the toolbar.
hosts.densityComfortableDesc: More detail per host: address, tags, and resource usage.
hosts.densityCompactDesc: One line per host, for longer lists.
hosts.displayTrayOnClick: Open actions on click (instead of hover)
hosts.actionsVisibilityDesc: Choose when host actions expand. Select click to restore the former click-to-expand behavior.
hosts.openOnDoubleClickDesc: Require a double click to open a host session instead of a single click
hosts.showFolderPathsDesc: Show the parent folder path above nested subfolder names. Subfolders stay indented either way.
hosts.focusExistingTabDesc: Clicking a host with an open tab switches to it instead of opening a new session. Ctrl/Cmd click, middle click, or "Open in new tab" always start a new one.
hosts.deleteHostsConfirm: Delete {{count}} host{{plural}}? This cannot be undone.
hosts.generateKeyPairDesc: Generate a new key pair, both private and public keys will be filled automatically.
hosts.enableAtLeastOneProtocol: Enable at least one protocol above to configure authentication and connection settings.

connect.label: Connect
connect.description: Open sessions only: terminal, remote desktop, file manager, tunnels and Docker. No access to the host configuration.

view.label: View
view.description: Connect, plus see the host configuration. Secrets are never shown.

edit.label: Edit
edit.description: View, plus modify non-authentication host settings. The owner's SSH authentication stays private and owner-only.

manage.label: Manage
manage.description: Edit, plus share the host with others, change permission levels and revoke access.

sharing.viewOnlyBanner: This host is shared with you by {{owner}} with view access. The configuration is read-only.
sharing.sharedEditBanner: This host is shared with you by {{owner}} with edit access. Changes apply to the real host; authentication references can only be changed by the owner.

sharing.authOverrideRequired: This host requires one of your saved credentials before you can connect.

transfer.noHostsConnectedHint: Add another SSH host with File Manager enabled in Host Manager.
transfer.destMustBeDirectory: Destination must be a directory for multi-item transfers
transfer.browsePathWillBeCreated: This folder does not exist yet. It will be created when the transfer starts.
transfer.browsePathError: Could not open this path on the destination host.
transfer.hostAuthRequired: Authentication required — open File Manager on this host first
transfer.parallelSegmentsHint: Large files are split into 256 MB chunks. Multiple lanes use separate connections (like starting several transfers) for higher total throughput.
transfer.jumpHostLimitation: Both hosts must be reachable from the Termix server. Direct host-to-host routing is not supported.
transfer.methodAutoHint: Picks tar or per-file SFTP based on file count, size, and compressibility. Single files always use streaming SFTP.
transfer.methodTarHint: Compress on source, transfer one archive, extract on destination. Requires tar on both Unix hosts.
transfer.methodItemSftpHint: Transfer each file individually over SFTP. Works on all hosts including Windows.
transfer.methodPreviewError: Could not preview transfer method. The server will still pick a method when you start.
transfer.methodItemSftpLimitation: Each file uses the same SFTP stream as a single-file copy, one after another. Progress is combined across all files, so the bar moves slowly during large files.

methodReason.tar_unavailable: Tar is not available on one or both hosts — per-file SFTP will be used instead.
methodReason.windows_host: A Windows host is involved — tar is not used.
methodReason.auto_multi_large: Auto: multiple files including a large file ({{largestSize}}) with compressible data — tar bundles into one transfer.
methodReason.auto_single_large_in_archive: Auto: one large file ({{largestSize}}) in this set — per-file SFTP.
methodReason.auto_many_incompressible: Auto: mostly incompressible data — per-file SFTP.
methodReason.auto_many_files: Auto: many files ({{fileCount}}) — tar reduces per-file overhead.
methodReason.auto_default: Auto: per-file SFTP for this set.

transfer.resumedHint: Reconnected to an active transfer started in another window.
transfer.transferCancelledCopyHint: Partial files may remain on the destination.

transfer.cleanupDestFilesPartial: Some partial files could not be removed
transfer.cleanupDestFilesNothing: Nothing to clean up on the destination
transfer.transferFailedRetryHint: Partial data was kept on the destination. Retry will resume when the connection is back.

auth.loginWithExternalDesc: Login using your configured external identity provider
auth.externalNotSupportedInElectron: External authentication is not supported in the Electron app yet. Please use the web version for OIDC login.

auth.passwordLoginDisabledDesc: Password login is disabled. Use a passkey or an external authentication provider.

auth.secondFactorNoUI: This second factor cannot be shown on this screen. Contact an admin.

donation.title: Enjoying Termix?
donation.body: Termix is free and open source, built and maintained by a two-person team in our spare time. If it's replaced a commercial tool you'd otherwise be paying for, a donation helps cover hosting costs and keeps development going. As of now, donations are crypto only.
donation.milestones: Donations also help fund the time to research and learn what's needed to build features like SAML and Kubernetes support. See the progress on the donate page.

dashboardTab.editModeInstructions: Drag cards to reorder · Drag the column divider to resize columns · Drag the bottom edge of a card to resize its height · Trash to remove

admin.brandingAppNameDesc: Shown on the login screen and browser tab. Leave empty to use "Termix".
admin.brandingTaglineDesc: Shown under the application name on the login screen. Leave empty to use the default tagline.
admin.brandingLogoDesc: PNG, JPEG or WEBP, up to 750 KB. Replaces the default icon on the login screen and browser tab.
admin.brandingLogoInvalid: Invalid image. Use a PNG, JPEG or WEBP file up to 750 KB.

admin.sslEmailDesc: Contact email for Let's Encrypt notifications and account.
admin.sslChallengeTypeDesc: How to prove domain ownership to Let's Encrypt.
admin.sslChallengeHttp: HTTP (webroot) - requires port 80 accessible from the internet
admin.sslChallengeDns: DNS (Cloudflare) - requires a Cloudflare API token
admin.sslCloudflareTokenDesc: Scoped token with Zone:DNS:Edit permission for your domain.
admin.sslInfoNote: After issuing or uploading a certificate, Termix will automatically enable HTTPS on SSL_PORT (default 8443) in addition to the existing HTTP port. Make sure that port is published/mapped to this container so it is reachable.
admin.sslManualDesc: Paste your existing certificate and private key, including a full chain if required by your CA.
admin.sslManualRequiresFields: Certificate and private key are required

admin.userAdminAccessDesc: Full access to all admin settings
admin.editUserDesc: Edit roles, admin status, sessions, and account settings.

macros.title: Macros
macros.description: Run a saved series of commands in a terminal, and react to what the server sends back.
macros.emptyHint: Create a macro to automate a terminal flow, like logging in, restarting a service, or answering prompts.
macros.name: Name
macros.nameRequired: Give the macro a name before saving
macros.deleteBody: "{{name}}" will be permanently deleted. This cannot be undone.
macros.needTerminal: Open and connect a terminal first
macros.noSteps: This macro has no steps yet. Add one below.

send.label: Send command
send.help: Types text into the terminal, the same as if you typed it.

wait.label: Wait for output
wait.help: Pauses until the server prints the text you name, like a password prompt.

delay.label: Pause
delay.help: Waits a fixed amount of time before the next step.

if.label: If output contains
if.help: Checks everything the server has printed so far, then runs one of two branches.

repeat.label: Repeat
repeat.help: Runs the steps inside it a set number of times.

send.pressEnterHelp: Turn this off to type text without submitting it.

match.useRegexHelp: Leave this off to match the text exactly as written.
match.invalidRegex: Not a valid regular expression, it will be matched as plain text

credentials:read.title: See your passwords and keys
credentials:read.consequence: It can read the stored secret for any host you can reach.

ssh:connect.title: Run commands on your servers
ssh:connect.consequence: Any command, on hosts you connect it to, with your access.

process:spawn.title: Run programs on this machine
process:spawn.consequence: Programs run on the Termix server itself, not on your hosts.

users:write.title: Create and change user accounts
users:write.consequence: It can add users and change their roles.

auth:provide.title: Handle sign in
auth:provide.consequence: It can add a login method, a second factor or an SSH sign-in type.

system:tls.title: Manage certificates
system:tls.consequence: It can request and replace the server certificate.

device:serial.title: Access serial and USB devices
device:serial.consequence: It can open a physical serial port on the machine running Termix.

hosts:write.title: Create and change hosts
hosts:write.consequence: It can add hosts and edit the ones you already have.

credentials:use.title: Connect to your servers
credentials:use.consequence: It cannot see your passwords or keys.

network:outbound.title: Reach the internet
network:outbound.consequence: It can send requests to outside services.

network:serve.title: Accept connections
network:serve.consequence: It opens a port on the Termix server.

network:broadcast.title: Send network broadcasts
network:broadcast.consequence: It can send packets to devices on the local network, such as a Wake-on-LAN signal.

users:read.title: See usernames and roles
users:read.consequence: Never password hashes, never two factor state.

events:core.title: Watch everything happening
events:core.consequence: Including activity from other users, not just yours.

notify:send.title: Send notifications
notify:send.consequence: Through the channels you have already set up.

audit:read.title: Read the audit log
audit:read.consequence: It can see who did what and when.

desktop:window.title: Open desktop windows
desktop:window.consequence: Only in the Termix desktop app.

hosts:read.title: See your host list
hosts:read.consequence: Names and addresses for hosts you can already see.

db:own.title: Store its own data
db:own.consequence: Kept in its own tables, separate from other plugins.

files:own.title: Store its own files
files:own.consequence: In its own folder on disk, separate from other plugins.

secrets:own.title: Store its own secrets
secrets:own.consequence: Encrypted by Termix. The plugin never holds the key.

settings:read-core.title: Read Termix settings
settings:read-core.consequence: Server settings, not your hosts or credentials.

ui:surface.title: Add its own screens
ui:surface.consequence: Tabs, panels and settings you can hide later.
